intended_object: The morphism module Hom_{H⁰(C)}(X, Y) = H⁰(Hom_C(X, Y)) of the homotopy category H⁰(C) of a DG category C over a commutative ring R: degree-0 cocycles of the Hom complex, modulo degree-0 coboundaries. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation (Keller, *Deriving DG categories*, §1).
explanation:
In this library, `DGCategory R C` is `EnrichedCategory (CochainComplex (ModuleCat R) ℤ) C`, i.e. a category enriched in cochain complexes of R-modules. That is the standard definition of a DG category. `dgHomComplex R X Y` is the enriched Hom object.

The definition takes Mathlib's `HomologicalComplex.homology` of that cochain complex at degree 0. With the cochain indexing (`ComplexShape.up ℤ`), this homology is ker(d⁰) / im(d⁻¹), which is exactly H⁰ of the Hom complex. The file confirms this:
- `dgHomotopyClass_eq_iff` shows that two cocycles have the same class exactly when their difference lies in the range of d⁻¹.
- `exists_dgHomotopyClass_eq` shows that every class has a cocycle representative.

The generality is the natural one: the definition works for any commutative ring R and any DG category, with the usual ℤ-grading. Mathlib has the general homology of complexes and a homotopy category of complexes over a preadditive category. It has no notion of a general DG category or of its H⁰, so there is no Mathlib counterpart that is more general or the same. No degenerate cases misbehave.
